title: Raised stem-stitch band
subtitle: Stem stitch worked over a laid foundation to create a padded ridge
excerpt: A raised stem-stitch band builds a firm, rounded ridge by laying a row of straight foundation stitches and then working rows of stem stitch over and across them without entering the fabric below. The result is a corded band that stands up from the surface, useful for stems, borders, and outlines that need dimension.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), raised embroidery chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 4 (1888), raised band entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A straight stitch or row of parallel stitches laid across the working area as a raised base for surface embroidery. The subsequent stitching wraps around the bar without entering the fabric.

heroPrompt: Raised stem-stitch band forming a thick curved stem in dark green wool on cream linen, showing the dimensional ridge, viewed from the side, daylight.

rather than along the fabric surface. The stem stitch rows lie across the bar at right angles; the needle only enters the fabric at the sides of the band, not through the padding.

items.label: Thread (foundation)
items.value: Crewel wool or thick perle cotton for the padding bars

items.label: Thread (stem stitch)
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 strands or fine crewel wool

items.label: Needle
items.value: Crewel needle size 7; tapestry needle size 24 for the surface stem stitch rows

content.text: Work a row of evenly spaced straight stitches across the band area, running perpendicular to the direction of the finished band.
Bring the working needle up at the left side of the band, just outside the first foundation bar.
Work stem stitch across the bar, with each stitch wrapping around the foundation threads. The needle enters the fabric at the sides of the band only.
Add rows of stem stitch side by side across the band. Each row packs tightly alongside the previous one, building the height of the raised band.

attrs.heading: When raised stem-stitch bands go wrong

items.symptom: The band is flat rather than raised
items.cause: The needle entered the fabric through the middle of the band instead of at the edges only.
items.fix: Keep the needle at the side edges only. The stem stitch should wrap over the top of the foundation bars, not stitch through the fabric beneath them.

items.cause: The stem stitch rows end at different points on each side.
items.fix: Always enter and exit the fabric at exactly the same line on each side. Mark the band edges on the fabric before starting.

content.text: Raised stem-stitch bands build thick stems in crewelwork designs, give sampler borders a rounded relief, and are used in goldwork as padding beneath cut metal thread.
